subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart, endpoints & rate limits
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Hi James,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — really enjoyed learning about Acme Health's ingestion pipeline and the high-throughput inference requirements for your triage workflows. As discussed, this thread is a quick recap and the recommended next steps for evaluating our Hosted API:

- Quickstart: I attached a short quickstart guide (redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf) that walks through creating an account, obtaining an API key, and calling the text-generation and embeddings endpoints. Should take ~30 minutes to run the sample workload.
- Endpoints & base URL: Hosted endpoints are hosted in our US region at https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1. The eval account I'll provision for you will have access to the text generation, chat, and embeddings endpoints.
- Rate limits & quotas: Default trial accounts are provisioned with 60 requests/min and 600k tokens/day. For production Hosted customers we offer configurable rate limits — we can increase to 300 req/min or add burst capacity depending on the plan.
- Data handling: Hosted API keeps customer data encrypted at rest; we provide SOC 2 docs and can discuss retention controls. Private VPC/on-prem is also an option if you need network isolation.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll provision a 14-day hosted eval account and share the API key + a small quota for performance testing.
2) You & Lina run the quickstart and a small synthetic load (I included a sample curl in the guide).
3) We sync after you’ve run the tests to review latency/throughput and discuss whether Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) or Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) makes sense for your SLA and compliance needs.

If that plan works, confirm the email(s) to provision access for (James, Lina) and I’ll send the credentials by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Aditya Rao

aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Hi Aditya,

Thanks — the plan sounds good. A couple of clarifying Qs before we start the quickstart:

1) Rate limits: when you say 60 req/min for trial, is that per API key or per account? Our ingesters are multi-threaded across 5 workers so we want to avoid unexpected 429s during tests.
2) Throughput: do you have any published guidance on tokens/sec or recommended concurrency for the hosted endpoints?
3) Data residency & retention: we’re required to keep logs within the US and have a 90-day retention policy for request/response logs. Will your hosted eval environment honor that?
4) Security docs: can you send SOC 2 and any encryption/KMS details?

Also Lina (cc) will own procurement — she might ask for a draft SOW once we’re comfortable with the performance.

Thanks,
James Miller
Director, Data Engineering | Acme Health
j.miller@acmehealth.com | (617) 555-9910

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Hi James — great questions. Answers below and a couple more helpful details to get you started:

1) Rate limits: trial rate limits are per-account (not per-key). I’ll provision a single account for Acme Health with 2 API keys. If you need higher concurrency during testing I can temporarily raise the account-level limit or provision separate sub-accounts we can route to different keys to prevent 429s.

2) Throughput guidance: for the hosted text-generation endpoint, a practical guideline is ~20-40 tokens/sec per concurrent request on our default instance type; throughput scales with concurrency and larger model choices. For embeddings, we typically see ~2000 vectors/sec on batched requests (batch size 64) on our hosted tier. I included a simple load pattern in the quickstart that ramps to 100 req/min across 5 workers.

3) Data residency & retention: our hosted US region stores logs in US-only storage by default. For the eval account I’ll set the request/response log retention to 90 days. For stricter requirements (long-term retention, audit isolation), Dedicated capacity or Private VPC is the recommended path.

4) Security docs: attached SOC 2 summary and a short note on our KMS integrations. Full SOC 2 report requires an NDA; our team can start that process if you want it.

Quickstart snippet (curl):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","prompt":"Summarize: The patient received...","max_tokens":256}'

Notes on limits: default trial: 60 req/min, 600k tokens/day. We can increase to 300 req/min or add burst capacity for short tests. If you want to test sustained higher throughput, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is the right next step — we can provide a pricing ballpark once we know target sustained RPS and model choice.

Next actions from my side:
- I’ll provision the 14-day hosted eval with the US region, set retention to 90 days, and attach the quickstart guide and SOC 2 summary (attached).
- Please run the quickstart with James/Lina’s team and share the basic perf numbers (p95 latency, tokens/sec, 95th percentile error rates).
- If you hit rate limits, reply here and I’ll bump the account limit for the test window.

I’m copying Marissa who’s our solutions lead — she can help with quant/benchmarking and any scripted load tests.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
